findings.place: Upper sphere, pale left interior contour and separate lower fragments
findings.h: Au crayon, deux sphères. La première : pôles $0$ (en haut) et $\infty$ (en bas), méridiens et équateur ; sur l'équateur, quatre petits cercles orientés autour de $1$, $i$, $-1$, $-i$ (étiquettes partiellement lisibles), reliés aux pôles par des chemins fléchés, certains en pointillé.
findings.ink: A thin pale interior curve lies between the dark left meridian to 1 and the dashed meridian to −i. Separate lower pale fragments approach the bottom oval. These are distinct from C’s two whole-sphere outline ellipses and its eight principal meridian segments; C has no matching interior construction strokes. Only visible portions are copied, with gaps retained and no new attachment or arrowhead. H names a general meridian family but makes no local claim about these pale traces, so it is not counted as differing. Main inspected and confirmed the new contextual crop.

findings.place: Upper sphere, close pale right interior contour pair
findings.h: Au crayon, deux sphères. La première : pôles $0$ (en haut) et $\infty$ (en bas), méridiens et équateur ; sur l'équateur, quatre petits cercles orientés autour de $1$, $i$, $-1$, $-i$ (étiquettes partiellement lisibles), reliés aux pôles par des chemins fléchés, certains en pointillé.
findings.ink: Two close pale pencil curves descend from near the upper oval inside the separate dashed route to −1. Their lower ends stop above the dashed back equator, rather than continuing to the marked −1 circle. C contains the quoted dashed principal path but not this separate pale pair. The new strokes have no heads, inferred continuations or cancellation. H’s general meridian description does not assert a local count or attachment and is not treated as an omission. Main confirmed both traces on the new crop.

findings.place: Lower sphere, downward head at the front vertical path’s i junction
findings.h: La seconde sphère : petit cercle orienté autour du pôle supérieur et autour de $\infty$ en bas ; sur l'équateur, cercles autour de $1$ et $-1$, points $-i$ et $i$ ; chemins marqués $\beta$, « $\beta$ relevé », « $\gamma$ relevé » (deux fois), le dernier avec la mention « $\gamma$ relevé, symétrique de \ill{} ».
findings.ink: At the front meridian/equator intersection, a small dark V points down toward i, with short slanting wings distinct from the vertical shaft. The existing upward head at the north oval also remains visible. The source therefore has the additional local head at the i end of this upper segment; the consolidated/C code supplied only the northward end head. Only this segment becomes double-ended. H’s general path-label prose makes no local directional claim. Main confirmed this precise V on the reused lower-equator crop.

findings.place: Lower sphere, pale stem/foot and detached point immediately right of the live i
findings.h: La seconde sphère : petit cercle orienté autour du pôle supérieur et autour de $\infty$ en bas ; sur l'équateur, cercles autour de $1$ et $-1$, points $-i$ et $i$ ; chemins marqués $\beta$, « $\beta$ relevé », « $\gamma$ relevé » (deux fois), le dernier avec la mention « $\gamma$ relevé, symétrique de \ill{} ».
findings.ink: Immediately to the right of the live i is an additional pale short descending stem with a bent foot, together with a small detached point above/right. It is separate from both the live letter and the farther-right curved meridian. Literal pale geometry is added; an i-like identification remains qualified, with no deletion or chronological status inferred from its light tone. C has only the quoted point and live i node. H’s synopsis of the labelled points does not locally describe this trace, so no H discrepancy is counted. Main confirmed the stem, foot and separate point on the existing crop.

notes: The upper sphere’s pale interior strokes are construction traces distinct from the principal meridians and outer outline. The reconstruction retains only visible upper portions and separate lower fragments; it does not close gaps or give them a mathematical direction.

The lower front upper meridian has an independently confirmed downward head at i as well as its northward head. This correction is local: the other meridian directions and the separate heads on the two lower polar rims were not harmonized to it.

The additional stem-and-point trace beside the live i is preserved as graphic ink. Its reading as i remains uncertain; neither faintness nor its position establishes cancellation or an earlier writing stage.

The extension close-up shows actual pointed heads on all four connectors, including the small filled head between F₂² and the cursive A₄. They remain ordinary arrows. The four upper-sphere arcs at 1 also retain their two end heads, including the looped pencil forms visible on the existing close-up.

Only the exact supplied H drawing descriptions were collated. They do not locally specify these new contour fragments, the front-i head or the pale i-like trace. All four audit findings therefore differ from C only; no unseen H drawing file or generic family synopsis was treated as evidence of a missing detail.

hand_log.habit: Pale interior construction curves and isolated letter-like traces remain alongside darker directed paths; their light tone alone does not establish a deletion or an earlier writing stage.
hand_log.universality: Local observation on the two sphere drawings; preserve visible geometry and qualify identification rather than inferring chronology.

coverage: Personally viewed the original once, then each native half once: top [0,0,1673,1295] and bottom [0,1059,1673,2354]. All labels, words, formulas, arrows and source graphic features were inspected against the complete consolidated draft and both full supplied witnesses before consulting current mark decisions or remaining-doubt descriptions. This included both sphere outlines, polar rims, equators, every principal meridian and small-circle arc, all marked points and labels, both beta leaders, eta annotations, the three mapping rows, full extension, loop relation and manuscript107. The four listed existing crops were inspected for concrete head/label/residue questions; one new contextual crop covered previously uncovered faint upper interior contours. All existing inventory elements were reviewed, with three graphic additions and one revised path description supplied in a complete order. No OCR, external research, TeX compilation or mathematical proof/computation was performed.
